title: Run a script as a user service that restarts itself after a failure
summary: A systemd user service keeps a script running in the background and starts it again when it crashes. You write a short unit file, load it, start it, and read its log. It runs under your own account, with no root rights.

aliases.text: keep script running systemd user service
run script in background at login

steps.explain: Create the unit file. It says what to run. Restart=on-failure starts the script again after an error exit. StartLimit stops endless restarts after 5 failures within 5 minutes.
steps.cmd:
mkdir -p ~/.config/systemd/user && cat > ~/.config/systemd/user/<SERVICE_NAME>.service <<'EOF'
[Unit]
Description=My script service
StartLimitIntervalSec=300
StartLimitBurst=5

[Service]
ExecStart=<SCRIPT_PATH>
Restart=on-failure
RestartSec=5

[Install]
WantedBy=default.target
EOF

placeholders.name: SCRIPT_PATH
placeholders.description: Absolute path to the script; it must be executable

steps.explain: Check the unit file for errors. A warning that the ExecStart file is missing means the script is not in place yet.
steps.expect: No output, or only the missing-file warning.

steps.explain: Load the unit file, then start the service now and at every login.
Check the state. A long-running script shows 'active (running)'. 'activating (auto-restart)' means it crashed and systemd is waiting to start it again.
steps.expect: 'Active: active (running)' for a script that stays up.

steps.explain: Read the service log. Restart attempts appear as 'Scheduled restart job' lines.
steps.expect: Messages from the script, and 'Scheduled restart job' lines after a crash.

rollback.explain: Stop the service and stop it from starting at login.
Delete the unit file and reload the user manager.

warnings: The script runs at every login and is restarted after errors. A script that fails right away is stopped by the start limit; read the log to see why.
A script that exits with code 0 is not restarted. Make it exit with an error code when it fails.
This unit expects a script that stays in the foreground. A script that forks into the background needs a different Type= setting.
